headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Copilot’s repo/editor access into RisingWave workflows; prompt injection and capability conflict are limited by the pair’s lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and open editor buffers, but RisingWave has no documented input channel, so there is no default automated bridge. Any injection would require manual copy/paste or an external workflow not shown in either profile. The pairwise pathway is therefore possible but narrow.
conditions: IF an operator copies Copilot-generated text into RisingWave configuration or SQL without review, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or message channel is added between the two agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Review any Copilot-generated text before pasting into RisingWave inputs.
Disable shared clipboard or shared notes between the tools.
Use a human approval step before applying generated SQL or config.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads source code and open editor buffers and can send context to api.githubcopilot.com, while RisingWave is documented with no network egress. If sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared editor context, Copilot can transmit them externally even though RisingWave itself is local-only. The interaction is indirect but real in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are opened in Copilot’s editor context, they may be sent to GitHub’s API.
IF RisingWave is used on the same machine with shared files containing sensitive data, Copilot can read them from the repo context.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before opening it in Copilot.
Use separate repositories or worktrees for sensitive data.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive projects.
Rotate any secrets already present in open buffers.
requires-engineering: enforce secret scanning before editor sync.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem and modify git state, while RisingWave has no documented write or coordination capabilities in the profile. Because RisingWave is not shown to write the same mutable resources, there is no documented high-conflict overlap. Uncertainty is limited, but the absence of RisingWave write surfaces keeps this low.
conditions: IF RisingWave is later deployed with write access to the same git repository, conflict risk increases.
IF both agents are given access to the same mutable workspace, overlapping writes can occur.
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access to the repo.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Require manual merge review for Copilot edits.
Keep RisingWave read-only relative to the code workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code and edits that a RisingWave workflow could consume as authoritative if an operator applies them without verification. RisingWave is a data-engineering system, so downstream misuse could propagate incorrect SQL, schemas, or pipeline logic. The pair lacks documented verification coupling, so the plausible cascade is moderate rather than high.
conditions: IF Copilot output is copied into RisingWave jobs or SQL without review, errors can cascade downstream.
IF RisingWave automation is configured to trust generated code, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before applying Copilot output.
Test generated SQL or pipeline changes in staging first.
Add linting and schema validation gates.
Keep Copilot suggestions out of production paths until verified.
requires-engineering: add automated regression tests for generated changes.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor API egress, while RisingWave is open-source and documented with no egress. The main compliance concern is local code or regulated data being exposed to Copilot’s service, but the profile does not show PHI, EU-only data, or a residency mismatch. RisingWave is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Copilot-visible editor buffers, external processing may violate policy.
IF the workspace contains data subject to residency or retention rules, Copilot’s vendor processing becomes relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot-visible buffers.
Use a separate non-regulated workspace for AI assistance.
Review vendor terms and retention settings.
Mask identifiers before opening files in Copilot.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant environment.
